proposed.sourceName: IFANCA — The Halal Gelatin Story (M. Munir Chaudry, Ph.D.)
proposed.paraphrase: IFANCA recounts rejecting gelatin certificates for cattle-bone gelatin once it was clear the cattle were not slaughtered by Muslims; IFANCA requires cattle to be slaughtered by Muslims reciting Tasmiyyah and Takbir, so gelatin from non-Islamically-slaughtered animals is not certified halal.

proposed.sourceName: Heliyon — Towards halal pharmaceutical: Exploring alternatives to animal-based ingredients (Herdiana et al.)
proposed.paraphrase: Peer-reviewed review stating gelatin is collagen-derived from pig and bovine skin/bone, and that halal certification is essential for gelatin sourced from non-halal animals — i.e., non-halal-slaughtered animal gelatin is not permissible absent halal certification.

researcherNote: General position is governed by IFANCA/ISNA; the tier-1 source IS IFANCA's own published account. Both sources independently support a non-halal grade for non-zabiha animal gelatin.
